collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 30 or older)

collection.description: A villager is happiest with their feet in the water as little fish nibble: do more of it, or wonder why.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (name1) has been noticing, lately, when (he/she) feels happiest. Not at feasts. Not when (he/she) finishes a big job. It's always the same small thing: sitting on the rocks at the end of the day with (his/her) feet in the water, watching the little fish nibble at (his/her) toes. That's it. That's the happiest part of (his/her) life.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (name1) decides that if that's the happiest part, (he/she) should do more of it. (He/she) starts going to the rocks every evening instead of every few days. (He/she) gets a little less done. (He/she) is a lot happier. People ask where (he/she) disappears to. "Fish," says (name1). Nobody understands. That's fine.

text_only.reason: the word's everyday sense (a thing, a sound or a person out of sight for a moment); nobody leaves the village -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (name1) wonders why. Why that, of all things? (He/she) tries to work it out: the quiet, the cool water, the fish who don't want anything from (him/her). (He/she) doesn't come up with an answer. (He/she) decides (he/she) doesn't need one. (He/she) goes to the rocks that evening and lets the fish nibble.
